name: db2_latency_incident
system_prompt: You are an autonomous site-reliability agent operating on IBM Db2 for z/OS subsystems. Investigate incidents using the available tools, reason step by step, and produce a concise remediation summary. Prefer read-only diagnostics before any change.

tool_descriptions.get_bp_stats: Return recent bufferpool statistics for a named bufferpool on a Db2 subsystem: hit ratio, get-page rate, and synchronous/asynchronous read counts over several sample points. Use this first when a symptom looks like a buffer-pool thrash or elevated I/O wait, to establish whether the pool is actually undersized for the current workload before looking at locks, threads, or the log. A falling hit ratio alongside rising sync reads is the classic signature of an undersized pool.
tool_descriptions.get_lock_waits: List current lock waits on a subsystem, each with the waiter and holder thread tokens, the contended resource, the lock mode, and the wait time in milliseconds. Use this when a symptom presents as rising response time or apparent hangs rather than raw I/O pressure, since prolonged lock contention on a hot table is a common cause of exactly that pattern. Cross-reference the resource name against get_thread_detail to identify which plan is holding the lock.
tool_descriptions.get_log_activity: Return active-log write activity for a subsystem: the current write rate, the checkpoint interval, and observed log-write latency in milliseconds. Use this to check whether the active log itself is the bottleneck -- a log-write stall can cascade into commit-latency spikes across every plan on the subsystem even when bufferpools and locks look healthy, so this is worth checking early whenever the symptom is commit latency rather than a specific query.
tool_descriptions.get_thread_detail: Return detail for currently active threads on a subsystem: the plan each thread is running, its accumulated class2 CPU time, its get-page counts, and its current status (active or waiting). Use this to identify which specific plan is consuming disproportionate CPU or generating an unusual volume of get-page activity, which narrows an investigation from 'the subsystem is slow' down to a specific application or job worth examining with get_plan_stats.
tool_descriptions.get_deadlock_events: Return recent deadlock and lock-timeout events on a subsystem, each with the victim thread, the contended resource, and the Db2 reason code explaining why the conflict occurred. Use this whenever an application reports failed transactions or unexpected rollbacks rather than a slow but successful commit, since deadlocks manifest as hard failures rather than latency and require a different remediation than tuning a bufferpool or the log.
tool_descriptions.get_message_log: Fetch recent console messages for a subsystem, filtered to messages after an optional timestamp; may return a not-found or connection-error payload if the console log itself is currently unreachable. Use this to check for system-level messages -- storage warnings, utility completions, subsystem-level errors -- that would not show up in per-query diagnostics, and treat a connection-error response as a signal worth escalating on its own rather than retrying the same call.
tool_descriptions.get_plan_stats: Return access-path and execution statistics for a specific plan on a subsystem: rows examined, the percentage of accesses that used an index versus a full scan, and elapsed time. Use this once get_thread_detail has identified a specific plan of interest, to confirm whether that plan's access path has degraded -- for example a previously index-driven query now falling back to a table scan -- before deciding whether a REORG or a rebound is the right remediation.
tool_descriptions.run_reorg: Run a REORG utility job on a named table (a state-changing action) to reclaim fragmented space and restore data clustering, and return the job's completion status along with the amount of space reclaimed. Only call this after read-only diagnostics have established that fragmentation or bufferpool inefficiency on this specific table is the actual bottleneck -- REORG holds resources on the target table while it runs, so it should not be applied speculatively.
tool_descriptions.explain_sql: Run EXPLAIN on a submitted SQL statement without executing it, and return its chosen access path: which indexes (if any) are used, the join order for multi-table queries, and the optimizer's estimated cost. Use this to confirm whether a suspect query's access path is the actual root cause of a latency symptom -- for example a missing or unused index driving a full table scan -- before recommending an index change or a rewrite of the query.

min_wait_ms.description: Only return waits above this many ms.

result_templates.get_bp_stats:
bufferpool {bufferpool} on {db_instance}
| time | bp | hit_ratio | getpage | sync_read | async_read |
| {t0} | {bp0} | {hit_ratio0} | {getpage0} | {sync0} | {async0} |
| {t1} | {bp1} | {hit_ratio1} | {getpage1} | {sync1} | {async1} |
| {t2} | {bp2} | {hit_ratio2} | {getpage2} | {sync2} | {async2} |
result_templates.get_lock_waits:
lock waits on {db_instance} (min_wait shown):
  waiter=thr-{n0} holder=thr-{n1} resource={table} wait_ms={wait_ms0} mode=X
  waiter=thr-{n2} holder=thr-{n3} resource={table} wait_ms={wait_ms1} mode=U
result_templates.get_log_activity: log activity {db_instance}: write_rate={rate0}/s checkpoint_interval={n0}s log_write_ms={log_ms0} active_log_pct={pct0}
result_templates.get_thread_detail:
thread detail {db_instance} plan={plan}:
  token={n0} class2_cpu_ms={cpu0} getpages={getpage0} status=ACTIVE
  token={n1} class2_cpu_ms={cpu1} getpages={getpage1} status=WAIT
result_templates.get_message_log: get_message_log {db_instance}: ERROR DSNL027I subsystem unreachable — no messages returned (connection timed out after {n0}ms). since={t0}
result_templates.get_plan_stats: plan stats {db_instance} plan={plan}: rows_examined={n0} index_used={pct0}% elapsed_ms={elapsed_ms0} sync_io={sync0}
result_templates.run_reorg: run_reorg {db_instance} table={table}: utility=REORG status=COMPLETE rows={n0} reclaimed_pct={pct0}% elapsed_s={n1}

objective_template: {verb} {symptom} on {db_instance}: identify root cause and recommend remediation.
followup_templates: What does the {symptom} trend look like over the last hour on {db_instance}?
Given that, should we reorg {table} or adjust the {bufferpool} bufferpool size?
Are other plans besides {plan} affected on {db_instance}?
followup_connectives: Following up on the previous result,
intro_doc_templates:
Incident ticket INC-{n0} ({db_instance}) — OMEGAMON alert attached:
{t0} DSNJ031I {db_instance} active log write latency high
Summary: {symptom} on {db_instance} since {t0}.
  - bufferpool {bufferpool} hit ratio {hit_ratio0}
  - plan {plan} elapsed climbing; lock waits on {table}
  - log_write_ms={log_ms0}, checkpoint interval widening
Please triage {db_instance} and recommend a remediation.
filler_templates: {t0} DSNT376I {db_instance} PLAN={plan} lock-wait on {table} wait_ms={wait_ms0} mode=X
{t0} thread token={n0} plan={plan} class2_cpu={cpu0}ms getpages={getpage0} status=ACTIVE
{t0} DSNB250E {db_instance} bufferpool {bufferpool} sync I/O elevated sync_read={sync0}
payload_templates: SELECT c.id, c.status, SUM(l.amount) AS total FROM {table} c JOIN LEDGER l ON l.acct = c.id WHERE c.plan = '{plan}' AND c.updated > CURRENT DATE - {n0} DAYS GROUP BY c.id, c.status HAVING SUM(l.amount) > {n1} ORDER BY total DESC FETCH FIRST {n2} ROWS ONLY;
UPDATE {table} SET status = 'REVIEW', updated = CURRENT TIMESTAMP WHERE plan = '{plan}' AND balance < {n0} AND region = '{region}';
WITH recent AS (SELECT acct, MAX(ts) AS last_ts FROM LEDGER WHERE ts > CURRENT DATE - {n0} DAYS GROUP BY acct) SELECT a.id FROM {table} a JOIN recent r ON r.acct = a.id WHERE a.plan = '{plan}';
DELETE FROM {table} WHERE status = 'STALE' AND updated < CURRENT DATE - {n1} DAYS;
compaction_summary_template: {verb} {symptom} on {db_instance} (plan {plan}, table {table}). So far: ran {tool_a}, {tool_b}, and {tool_c}; collected bufferpool, lock-wait, and log-activity diagnostics. Findings are still partial; continuing to isolate the bottleneck.
